name: Charles Babbage
knownFor: For designing the first mechanical computers
summary: Babbage grew frustrated with error-prone human calculation and spent decades designing machines that could compute automatically. His Analytical Engine carried the blueprint for every computer that followed.
contributions: Difference Engine — the first automatic mechanical calculator
Analytical Engine — the first design for a general-purpose computer
Introduced punched-card input and a separate 'store' and 'mill'
Worked with Ada Lovelace, who wrote programs for the engine

note.body: The engine was never finished, but the idea outlived the brass.

name: Ada Lovelace
knownFor: For writing the first computer program
summary: Translating a paper on Babbage's Analytical Engine, Lovelace added notes three times longer than the original — including an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, widely regarded as the first published computer program.
contributions: First published algorithm intended for a machine (1843)
Foresaw that computers could compose music and manipulate symbols
Called her approach 'poetical science'
The Ada programming language is named in her honour

note.body: The Engine weaves algebraic patterns, just as the Jacquard loom weaves flowers.

name: Alan Turing
knownFor: For the Turing machine and breaking Enigma
summary: Turing gave computation a mathematical definition before a single electronic computer existed, then used those ideas to help break the German Enigma cipher during World War II.
contributions: The Turing machine — a formal model of computation (1936)
Solved the Entscheidungsproblem, proving some problems are undecidable
Led codebreaking work at Bletchley Park
Proposed the Turing test for machine intelligence (1950)
Modelled morphogenesis, how patterns form in nature

note.body: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs doing.

name: Dennis Ritchie
knownFor: For creating C and co-creating Unix
summary: Ritchie designed the C language and, with Ken Thompson, built Unix. Between them they shaped the operating systems, languages and tooling that almost all modern software still rests on.
contributions: Created the C programming language (1972)
Co-created Unix at Bell Labs with Ken Thompson
Co-wrote 'The C Programming Language' — the K&R book
Helped design Plan 9 and the Inferno operating systems
Received the Turing Award in 1983

note.body: C is quirky, flawed, and an enormous success.

name: Ken Thompson
knownFor: For creating Unix and co-creating Go
summary: Thompson wrote the first Unix in a few weeks while his wife was away, then spent the next fifty years quietly changing how software is built — from B and grep to UTF-8 and Go.
contributions: Co-created Unix and wrote the first version (1969)
Created the B language, a direct ancestor of C
Wrote tools like grep, ed and the original shell
Co-designed UTF-8 with Rob Pike
Co-created the Go programming language

note.body: You can't trust code that you did not totally create yourself.

name: Bjarne Stroustrup
summary: Stroustrup wanted the speed of C with the structure of Simula. The result was C++, the language that carried object-oriented programming into systems, games and everything in between.
contributions: Created C++ (originally 'C with Classes', 1979)
Championed RAII and the zero-overhead principle
Wrote 'The C++ Programming Language'
Continues to guide the ISO C++ standard

note.body: C makes it easy to shoot yourself in the foot; C++ makes it harder, but when you do, it blows your whole leg off.

name: Richard Stallman
knownFor: For founding GNU and the Free Software Foundation
summary: Stallman launched the GNU Project to build a free operating system, then wrote the GPL to keep it free. His ideas turned software freedom from a slogan into a legal and social movement.
contributions: Founded the GNU Project (1983)
Wrote the GNU General Public License (GPL)
Created GNU Emacs and the GNU Compiler Collection
Founded the Free Software Foundation (1985)
Defined the four freedoms of free software

note.body: Free software is a matter of liberty, not price.

name: James Gosling
summary: Gosling led the team that built Java around a radical promise: write once, run anywhere. A decade later the language was running everything from phones to enterprise backends.
contributions: Created the Java programming language and the JVM (1995)
Lead architect of Sun Microsystems' Java platform
Built the 'Oak' project that became Java
Wrote Gosling Emacs

note.body: Write once, run anywhere — then debug everywhere.

name: Linus Torvalds
summary: Torvalds released a hobby kernel in 1991 and let the world build on it. Fourteen years later he wrote Git in a matter of weeks, giving that same world a better way to collaborate.
contributions: Created the Linux kernel (1991) and still maintains it
Created Git for version control (2005)
Popularised the open-source, distributed development model
Received the Millennium Technology Prize (2012)

note.body: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.

name: John Carmack
knownFor: For DOOM, Quake and real-time 3D engines
summary: Carmack's id Tech engines made PC games a technical frontier. DOOM and Quake pushed 3D rendering further than the hardware was supposed to allow, and he later turned to virtual reality.
contributions: Built the Doom and Quake engines at id Software
Pioneered real-time 3D rendering techniques
Popularised the fast inverse square root
Released id's engine source under the GPL
Became CTO of Oculus VR

note.body: Story in a game is like a story in a porn movie — it's expected, but not that important.
